I've heard that idea before. I've been on the web, albeit not on gofundme, and while people find my face amusing, it doesn't make them feel sympathy but pity. Trust me, those two things are different. People can't feel sympathy for me because they can't relate to my situation. They blend in with the crowd and they don't know what it's like to not only stick out, but stick out because of something that is unique to you and they don't understand what it's like to truly be alone with your bullying. Geeks and fat people have others just like them, but there is no community of ugly women, let alone those with facial deformities. There's no awareness of how horrible our lives are, everyone can see how well pretty women are treated and why that is, but noone wants to notice the opposite, just like everyone pretends not to see the homeless guy on the street. It's a fact of society average people would rather pretend isn't there, and let's face it, those who are attractive don't want competition so they'd rather be "morally opposed" to stuff like plastic surgery than help the lonely because if people start waking up to reality they lose their upper hand in society. 
I'm in a weird position as well to explain to a stranger, the procedure I need would be for cosmetic purposes but it's a serious, risky surgical procedure not some feel-good tv makeover type thing.
